title: Spin nematic liquid crystal and scalar spin chirality in tetragonal lattice YbMnBi$_2$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, Pengcheng Dai
abstract: A spin nematic order, analogous to the nematic liquid crystal, characterizes the spontaneous breaking of spin-space rotational symmetry while preserving time-reversal ($T$) symmetry. In contrast, scalar spin chirality (SSC), a composite three-spin order, breaks $T$ symmetry and is known to induce an anomalous Hall effect (AHE). Although a spin nematic phase has been suggested in frustrated magnets and the square-lattice iridate, how it might affect magnetotransport properties is unknown. Here we use polarized neutron scattering to show that tetragonal $A$MnBi$_2$ ($A$ = Ca, Yb) is a strictly $c$-axis-aligned collinear antiferromagnet (C-type), with $T_N \approx 270$ K and 290 K, respectively. On cooling from 450 K to $T_N$, low-energy spin excitations in YbMnBi$_2$ spontaneously change from isotropic to anisotropic in spin space within the tetragonal plane, forming a dynamic spin nematic phase around 400 K due to heavy Yb-induced spin-orbit coupling, before gapping out below $T_N$. Similar measurements on CaMnBi$_2$ reveal isotropic paramagnetic scattering without a spin nematic phase above $T_N$. Under an in-plane magnetic field, the Yb$^{3+}$ moments may interact with the dynamic spin nematic phase to induce nonzero SSC, giving rise to AHE and an anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) in YbMnBi$_2$ that are absent in CaMnBi$_2$ above $T_N$. A symmetry-based Ginzburg-Landau analysis shows that coupling terms between the nematic order and SSC are allowed under an external magnetic field, which could explain the rapid increase of AHE with field in YbMnBi$_2$. Our results provide compelling evidence for dynamic SSC-induced AHE and ANE in the paramagnetic phase of a compensated collinear antiferromagnet, opening a new avenue for the physics of composite spin orders and room-temperature spintronics without magnetic order.
summary: The authors investigate the interplay between spin nematic order and scalar spin chirality in $	ext{YbMnBi}_2$ using polarized neutron scattering. They find that $	ext{YbMnBi}_2$ exhibits a high-temperature dynamic spin nematic phase, which couples with an external magnetic field to induce anomalous Hall effects (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effects (ANE). This provides strong evidence for composite spin orders driving room-temperature spintronic phenomena in antiferromagnets.
main_problem: The study investigates the relationship between spin nematic order, scalar spin chirality (SSC), and anomalous magnetotransport effects in tetragonal magnetic compounds.
main_result: In $	ext{YbMnBi}_2$, a dynamic spin nematic phase exists above $T_N$ that couples with an external field to induce measurable AHE and ANE, phenomena absent in the analogous $	ext{CaMnBi}_2$.
method: The research employs polarized neutron scattering (LPA) to probe spin excitations and measures magnetotransport properties like the Anomalous Hall Effect (AHE).
model_or_system: The system under study is the tetragonal lattice $	ext{YbMnBi}_2$ compared to $	ext{CaMnBi}_2$, which are characterized as collinear antiferromagnets. The physics involves complex spin orders: nematicity (breaking rotational symmetry) and SSC (a three-spin, time-reversal symmetry breaking order).
key_observables: Spin excitation anisotropy ($M_a$ vs $M_b$ vs $M_c$), AHE/ANE magnitude, and the temperature dependence of magnetic scattering intensities.
important_parameters: Critical temperatures like $T_N \approx 270-290	ext{ K}$ and a nematic crossover temperature around $400	ext{ K}$; external magnetic field strength ($B$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed AHE/ANE in $	ext{YbMnBi}_2$ is due to coupling between the dynamic spin nematic phase and SSC, which is not present in $	ext{CaMnBi}_2$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate temperature dependence of scattering cross sections ($\sigma^{	ext{SF}}$) showing changes in magnetic moment anisotropy across $T_N$ and $T_S$, alongside plots detailing the AHE response vs. field for both compounds.
paper_structure: The paper establishes background on spin nematicity and SSC, uses polarized neutron scattering to characterize the distinct dynamic spin nematic phase in $	ext{YbMnBi}_2$ above $T_N$, confirms the collinear AFM structure via multiple measurements, and finally links this high-temperature nematic state to field-induced AHE/ANE.
why_interesting: This work connects exotic magnetic orders (nematicity) observed through neutron scattering directly to measurable transport phenomena (AHE), providing a concrete platform for studying emergent quantum magnetotransport effects in correlated materials.
